At 12.30 p.m. 1/12/37, S. I. Chou Chung Ming
(周忠明)(Gordon Road), telephoned the station from
his home at 45 Yeaping Terrace, Yenping Road, stating
that he was detaining two male Chinese at his home
suspecting them to be fraudulently soliciting con-
tributions for comforts for the Chinese Army.

Detectives were dispatched to the scene
and brought to the station the 1st and 2nd described
on Sheet 1. The 1st described was wearing an
amulet bearing the characters of the "National
Crisis Youths Service Group", and in his possession
was found a contribution receipt book bearing the
chop of the same organization.

From enquiries made by D. S. I. Cumming, D. S.
I. Chu Mang Wei and C. D. C. 239, it was ascertained
that the 1st described was a collector employed by
the above organization at 431 Kiangse Road until
15th November 1937, on which date it voluntarily wound
up its affairs. He was at that time in pos-
session of an amulet and two receipt books which
he failed to return. Since that date he admits
that on divers dates he, in concert with one or
other of the persons described on Sheet 1, collected
the sum of about $50.00 from various householders
in the Settlement and divided the proceeds with
his accomplices. A correct check-up cannot be
made, however, as the receipt book stub contains
many fictitious names and amounts contributed
which the suspect himself entered with a view to
impressing his victims. As the stub bears no

1937年12月1日下午12时30分，巡佐周忠明（Chou Chung Ming）（戈登路）从其位于延平路延平里45号的家中致电巡捕房，称其在家中扣留了两名中国男子，怀疑他们以欺诈手段为中国军队募集慰劳品捐款。

侦探被派往现场，并将第1页所述的第一和第二号嫌疑人带至巡捕房。第一号嫌疑人身佩戴有“国难青年服务团”字样的徽章，并在其身上搜出盖有该组织印章的捐款收据簿。

经副探长卡明（Cumming）、副探长朱孟伟（Chu Mang Wei）及华籍侦探主任 239 号询问后查明，第一号嫌疑人直至1937年11月15日一直受雇于上述位于江西路431号的组织担任收款员，该日该组织自愿结束事务。当时他持有一枚徽章和两本收据簿，未予归还。自那以后，他承认在不同日期，他与第1页所述的其他一人或多人合谋，向租界内的各住户募集了约50.00美元，并与同伙瓜分所得。然而，由于收据簿存根包含许多虚构的姓名和捐款金额（系嫌疑人本人为给受害者留下深刻印象而填写），无法进行准确核对。由于存根上没有

members of the Shanghai Municipality National Crisis Youths'
Service Group(國難青年服務團) in the afternoon of October 28

of cakes for the Chinese soldiers now holding out in a godown
of North Thibet Road, it is learned that in all $34.60 was
raised and later remitted to the Chinese Chamber of Commerce
which organization will arrange for the purchase of food stuff

October 21, 1937. Afternoon Translation.

The "Kuo Nai Tsing Nyi" (國難青年), a weekly, Volume 1,
Issue No. 2, published on October 17 the following article
written by one Tsai Yu-hong (蔡元鴻) :-

DEVELOPMENTS BROUGHT ABOUT BY OUR EXTENSIVE PROPAGANDA
ON THE ANNIVERSARY OF NATIONAL INDEPENDENCE DAY

All of us, seven in number, assembled on a
certain street before 8 a.m. that day (the National
Independence Day) despite the heavy rain. We all carried
booklets, slogans, posters, banners and other articles
for our propaganda work on that day, the anniversary of
the Double Tenth.
On our way to the waterworks refugees camp
and just as we were posting up slogans and distributing
manifestoes at the intersection of Chengtu Road and Avenue
Foch, a black vehicle suddenly dashed towards us and we
were forced to scatter. In the meantime, a certain Chinese,
under the protection of the foreign "lords," haughtily
approached and shouted to us: "Hello, friends! This is a
British Settlement. How dare you create disturbance to
the menace of the order of the Settlement?"
"We do not care whether our action constitutes
a disturbance or not," retorted one of our comrades named
Chiang (). "We only know that this is Chinese territory,
therefore, why should we not post slogans inasmuch as the
posting of handbills and slogans does not constitute an
offence? My friend, have you no warm blood? Are you not
a Chinese? Can you remain looking patiently at the invasion
of your country by the enemy? The whole nation is at
present waging a war of bitter resistance against the enemy!
My friend, please mind your own business!"
"What, mind my own business!" replied the
man under foreign protection. "Have I not the right to
interfere?....Huh! Speak no more; go to the Station!"
"Alright," we all shouted.
We unhesitatingly jumped on the car, because
we had nothing to fear for we were working for our country.
Upon arrival at the Station, we were subjected
to an unnecessary interrogation and were thus deprived of
our freedom for no less than four hours in the Charge Room,
but it in no way weakened our determination.
"Had we committed any offence? No, we had
done nothing offensive. Then, how was it that we could
be arbitrarily arrested?"
I cannot find an appropriate reply. Only
those who are spineless and soulless can know the reply.
After we had been released, we made our
way to the waterworks refugees camp on XX Road.

周刊《国难青年》第一卷第二期，于10月17日出版，刊登了蔡元鸿撰写的一篇文章：-

我们在双十节国庆日广泛宣传所引发的进展

尽管那天（国庆日）大雨倾盆，我们七人仍在上午8点前在某条街道集合。我们都携带了小册子、标语、海报、横幅及其他用于当天双十节纪念宣传工作的物品。
在前往自来水厂难民收容所的路上，正当我们在成都路与福煦路路口张贴标语和散发传单时，一辆黑色汽车突然向我们冲来，迫使我们四散躲避。与此同时，一名在某些外国“老爷”庇护下的中国人傲慢地走近，对我们喊道：“喂，朋友们！这里是英租界。你们怎敢制造扰乱，威胁租界的秩序？”
“我们不在乎我们的行为是否构成扰乱，”我们一位姓蒋（）的同志反驳道。“我们只知道这是中国领土，既然张贴传单和标语并不构成犯罪，我们为何不能张贴？朋友，你没有热血吗？你不是中国人吗？你能耐心地坐视敌人入侵你的国家吗？目前全国正在进行艰苦的抗战！朋友，请管好你自己的事！”
“什么，管好我自己的事！”那个受外国人庇护的人回答道。“难道我没有权利干涉吗？....哼！别说了，去巡捕房！”
“好，”我们齐声喊道。
我们毫不犹豫地跳上了车，因为我们无所畏惧，我们是在为国家工作。
到达巡捕房后，我们受到了不必要的审问，因此在拘留室被剥夺自由长达四个多小时，但这丝毫没有削弱我们的决心。
“我们犯了什么罪吗？没有，我们没有做任何冒犯之事。那么，我们怎么会遭到任意逮捕？”
我找不到合适的回答。只有那些没有骨气、没有灵魂的人才知道答案。
获释后，我们前往XX路上的自来水厂难民收容所。

fluently. He is a Shanghai resident of long standing and
